### The problem

The issue appears after my dad shared his Roborock with my account and this integration is trying to reach locally his robot and it crashes (I'm not on that network and there is no response). And I couldn't test if the device is offline (like I have another Roborock in a summer house that's turned off when no one is there) if this integration fails too -but I assume that it fails too-.

I would say a good solution for this is to be able to select which device you want to add to HA, because now it's trying to add 3 devices, which just one is on my house. The other two devices are just shared devices with me.

I am having the same issue since 2023.8.3 .   I have 1 roborock and 1 shared roborock linked to my roborock account.  It works well in HA 2023.8.2 and before, but failed to load after upgrading to 2023.8.3.

> If anyone is willing to share a robot with me - I can take a look into this. As it should be working. Your shred vacuum should connect with the online version of our code

the problem of sharing a device is there is no option in Roborock app to remove access unfortunately. You can use your own Roborock account and have a home-assistant in different network (VPN connected or guest network), it's the same result, the integration will try to reach your robot using the private IP and it'll crash in the same way (timeout bc IP address is unreachable).

If you want to have a shared robot you can create a 2nd Roborock account (must be in the same region otherwise it'll say account doesn't exist) and share yours with that account and try it.

I've tried:

1) Connecting with my account using a personal hotspot and not the same wifi - it successfully connects using the online api
2) Creating a new account, sharing my vacuum with this new account, and then connecting to that account - still not on my wifi and I connect successfully with the online api.

Besides - at this point of the code, it is not trying to communicate with your device locally. It is using the cloud api to get the network information, but it fails, which should not be the case if you are able to communicate with it through the app.

One of my shared devices is offline certainly. I have 3 robots on my account, 2 online (1 shared), one offline (shared).

Yes, I am able to use the robots using the Roborock app without any issues
